ambiguities.text: The specification does not clarify what happens if an EIP attempts to use an address in the RIP-reserved range.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume that EIP process will enforce the reservation by rejecting EIPs that propose precompiles in 0x100-0x1ff. This is a governance assumption.

ambiguities.text: The term 'RIP process' is used without a clear definition of what constitutes a valid RIP.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume RIP refers to the Rollup Improvement Proposal process as defined by L2 ecosystem governance, analogous to EIP for L1.

implicit_assumptions.description: Assumes that L2 rollups will respect the reserved range and not deploy conflicting precompiles within their own address spaces.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Multiple L2s could deploy different precompiles at the same RIP address, causing cross-rollup interoperability issues.

implicit_assumptions.description: Assumes 256 addresses (0x100-0x1ff) will be sufficient for all RIP precompile needs.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Future RIP proposals may exceed available address space, requiring additional reservations or address reuse.
